title: Wakeword backend failures are silently fire-and-forgotten
reasoning: wakewordDetected starts the backend transport request and discards the returned promise without a catch or any caller-visible completion signal. If the SDK-hosted Electron backend rejects or is unavailable, the renderer cannot observe or handle the failure, and the runtime may produce an unhandled rejection depending on the transport implementation.
reproduction: Make createDesktopBackendTransport(null).wakewordDetected reject, then call DesktopVoiceRuntimeClient.wakewordDetected and observe that the client neither reports failure nor handles the rejected promise locally.
recommendation: Either return the promise from wakewordDetected so callers can handle failure, or catch and route the error through the renderer's established runtime logging/error-reporting path.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are provided for this feature, and there is no evidence of a contract test asserting how wakeword transport failures are surfaced.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that stubs wakewordDetected to reject and asserts the client either returns the rejection to the caller or logs/reports it through the chosen error channel.
minimumFixScope: Change desktopVoiceRuntimeClient wakewordDetected error handling contract and cover the rejection path.
